outcome.technical: Diagnosis: the product was right and the case depended on runner speed. On windows cp1252 2 the x-block was killed by the 2s deadline before python start-up, the _harness import (with a cold per-run pycache) and staged_main dispatch had reached its print. So the partial line was legitimately empty. The rest worked: the replay ran past the deadline, x was named as timed out, y as refused, 0/2. A product fault would have failed every windows leg, but only one failed. Fix, in the tt3c case of tools/sweep-selftests.py only (no product function changed): (1) the split-hang fixture is built by tt_hang(delay). It sleeps delay, prints the partial line, then creates a witness file (tt_box/tt-printed, outside the child's watched scratch and home) and hangs. split-quick is built from the same template without the hang, and still holds no time.sleep, as tt3b asserts. (2) tt3c runs the suite with deadline 1, 2, 4, 8 and stops at the first run whose witness exists. Run 1 delays the print 2.0s past its 1s deadline on purpose, so every runner judges a run that printed nothing. (3) On every run it asserts that ok is False, that x is named as not finishing within Ns, that y is refused with that run's own deadline, that PASS ty1 is absent, that the output ends 0/2, and that the run took under 30s. A witnessed run must carry the partial line exactly once; a run with no witness at most once, because the print comes before the witness write. If no run is witnessed the case fails, naming every deadline tried. Evidence: (a) `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --selftest` in the task tree: ALL PASS 153/153, exit 0, runs [(1s, not printed, 1.1s), (2s, printed, 2.1s)]. (b) Task gate `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tools/sweep-selftests.py`: '1/1 files ok, 153 cases', exit 0. (c) Throwaway-copy mutations: partial dropped in block_entry gave tt3c+tt3d red (151/153, exit 1); partial duplicated gave tt3c+tt3d red (151/153); a 20s delay so no run ever prints gave tt3c red (152/153), every deadline tried listed; the slow runner (2.5s delay) gave green at the 4s deadline. (d) ruff check: All checks passed; vermin -t=3.8-: no violations; _output_lints.prose_number_claims('.') = [] and house_style_violations() = []. (e) `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test__refs.py`: '1/1 files ok, 292 cases' (tail through a pipe; the sweep line is the evidence). Own-tests command could-not-run, verbatim: '[run-test-gate] no phase 'P145' in this manifest', exit 2. My tree's manifest is HEAD f10ed750, and P145 is still uncommitted in the project tree. Wall time of the suite: 30.6s before, 32.1s and 32.2s after (each measured once, same machine). Run 1 adds about 1.1s. Dependants: every listed file (.claude/skills/before-you-claim/evals/evals.json, .github/sweep-costs.json, .github/workflows/ci.yml, plugins/audit/scripts/_output.py, governance/_runner_collects.py, governance/_runner_output.py, governance/stamp-verification.py, manifest/_filed_returns.py) and every listed name (budget_line, coverage_findings, default_jobs, file_timeout) is still correct. The diff touches only fixture text and the body of tt3c inside the selftest; no function signature, CLI flag, output line, cost rule or timeout rule changed. The one effect any of them can see is the suite's own seconds in .github/sweep-costs.json, about 1s more, well inside its timeout; I did not re-record the table. Brief mismatch, for the orchestrator: the launch message described prove-gates.py pw5/pw6/pw13 (that is P145.2's brief) and said not to touch sweep-selftests.py. But it named brief-145-1.md as the authority, and that brief, the manifest's files and this submit block all make P145.1 the tt3c / tools/sweep-selftests.py task. I followed the brief, in my own tree claude-plugins-P145.1, and did not touch prove-gates.py.
outcome.descriptive: tt3c's verdict no longer depends on how fast a runner starts a process: a witness file says whether the killed block printed, and the deadline doubles until it has, so the slow windows leg that failed it now passes the same assertions.
